title: First time improvising at a Dansville talent contest
summary: He lost his place reading a written solo, improvised, and loved it; a school teacher later sparked his jazz interest.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: At some point did your father say, especially to you and John on trumpet, that, okay now it’s time to play music that’s not on the page, and how did he describe that?

I’ll tell you, my first experience with that, because we never did that. What happened was we always read the solos that were written in there. They were little note solos that were written. And the first time I remember we were playing a talent contest in Dansville, New York with the family band, I’ve even got a picture of the night somewhere where somebody took it from the audience. And I had to stand up and read the transcribed solo. And I looked down and I lost my place so I just started improvising. And after the set I remember we finished and I went offstage to my two brothers and I said, “Man, I just made up my own stuff and it felt really great.” I was really enthused about it. And that was the first time I ever had really improvised on my own. And then from then on, it didn’t last that long, the spark, I mean we kept doing it as kids. And it didn’t really kind of hit me until I got into high school that that’s the direction I wanted to go in. And it wasn’t my father, it was my school music teacher that really started the spark about jazz.
